slides.head: Is a ₦2 stock cheap?
slides.body: Not by itself. Here's the test.

slides.head: Ask what you're paying for.
slides.body: Each share gets a slice of the company's profit: earnings per share (EPS).

slides.head: Stock X: ₦2 a share, earns ₦0.05
slides.body:
You pay 40 times what it earns.
That's a P/E of 40.

slides.head: Stock Y: ₦200 a share, earns ₦25
slides.body:
You pay 8 times what it earns.
That's a P/E of 8.

slides.head: The ₦200 share is the cheaper one.
slides.body: But a low P/E can also be a warning sign, so always check why it's low.

slides.head: Know the stock before you buy the story.
slides.body: Learn to read the numbers, free, at moloneystreetre.com
